claims.text: The ball-milled Mg-Al-Ti-V-Fe-Co powder is a supersaturated BCC solid solution.
The ball-milled powder has a high defect density and may contain surface oxide contamination.
An SPS temperature window of 850–950 °C optimizes precipitation of a continuous nanocrystalline intermetallic network.
The proposed intermetallic network consists of Mg-rich, Ti/Fe-rich, Mg-Al-Ti, or Fe-V-rich secondary phases.
The secondary intermetallic precipitates form a percolating network at grain boundaries.
Temperatures above 800 °C provide sufficient atomic diffusion to decompose the metastable BCC solid solution.
Decomposition of the BCC solid solution produces thermodynamically stable intermetallic phases.
The intermetallic precipitates nucleate preferentially at grain boundaries.
The grain-boundary intermetallic network slows outward Mg diffusion and inward oxygen diffusion.
Restricted Mg and oxygen diffusion promotes formation of a dense, adherent, protective passive film.
The precipitate network suppresses matrix coarsening and Mg loss.
SPS within the proposed window produces a bulk alloy exceeding 98% theoretical density.
Precipitation strengthening and grain-boundary pinning significantly increase hardness.
Material sintered within the proposed window has better oxidation and corrosion resistance than material sintered below 800 °C or above 950 °C.
Sintering below 800 °C provides insufficient driving force for densification and bulk formation.
Sintering above 950 °C causes Mg loss and disruption of the diffusion-barrier network.
The mechanism fails above 980 °C because significant Mg evaporation changes local stoichiometry.
Mg evaporation at excessive temperature dissolves the protective intermetallic network.
Loss of the protective intermetallic network leads to a porous, non-protective oxide scale.
Parabolic oxidation kinetics would indicate diffusion control, whereas linear kinetics would indicate surface-reaction-limited behavior and absence of an effective diffusion barrier.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome places the onset of Mg loss and barrier disruption above 950 °C, whereas the boundary says the mechanism fails only when temperature exceeds 980 °C. The status of the 950–980 °C interval is therefore inconsistent or insufficiently defined.
